COREUniformityThe rule behind the rules.

CORE-01

Write new code the way the existing code is written. Uniformity outranks personal preference.

README.md

Everything should look uniform.

CORE-02

An unwritten convention is still a convention. File names, CSS classes, formatting and even attribute order follow the same systematic approach — silence is not permission.

README.md
CORE-03

A selectable option is always {value, label} — value is internal, label is displayed. Select, dropdown, radio, tabs alike.

value_label.md
{value: <internal>, label: <display>}
CORE-04

Opposites come from the established pairs, not from invention.

README.md
construct/destruct  create/destroy
open/close          begin/end
start/finish        first/last
next/previous       get/put
src/dest            source/destination
res/rej             resolve/reject
req/res             request/response
setup/teardown      push/pull
enabled/disabled    import/export

NAMENaming grammarVerb morphology decides function or data.

NAME-01

Functions are verb phrases, data are noun phrases. Each assignment reads as a sentence — the verb performs, the noun holds.

README.md
const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);
NAME-02

English verb morphology is the marker. An imperative verb makes a function; a past participle makes data. Prepositions are neutral — the verb form decides the side.

naming_markers.md
items_sort_by_time(items)   // function
items_sorted_by_time        // data
NAME-03

A bare _by_ name is always data, never a function. Lookup is bracket access, not a call.

naming_markers.md
user_by_id[id]     ✓ right
user_by_id(id)     ✗ wrong
NAME-04

Plurality of the first word states lookup cardinality — what one key returns, not how big the container is.

var_names.md
user_by_id[id]                    // User
users_by_role[role]               // User[]
children_by_parent_id[parent_id]  // Node[]
NAME-05

_sorted_by_ marks data of the same shape, reordered. The participle survives here because it carries what shape alone cannot.

naming_markers.md
items_sorted_by_time   // Item[], still an array
NAME-06

_per_ marks a ratio or a rate.

naming_markers.md
clicks_per_visit
NAME-07

The operations that produce those shapes are _group_by_, _sort_by_ and _index_by_. The criterion follows the verb.

naming_markers.md
users_index_by_id(users)     // user_by_id
users_group_by_role(users)   // users_by_role
items_sort_by_time(items)    // items_sorted_by_time
NAME-08

Use _from_ only when something is computed, parsed or constructed — result first, source last.

naming_markers.md
user_from_token(token)
date_from_timestamp(ts)
tree_from_array(rows)
NAME-09

_from_ never means lookup. A lookup disguised as construction is wrong.

naming_markers.md
user_from_id(id)   ✗ wrong
user_by_id[id]     ✓ right
NAME-10

_to_ is for method position only, where the source is the receiver.

naming_markers.md
tree.to_json()
NAME-11

_to_ is banned in data names — id_to_name is only a second spelling of name_by_id.

naming_markers.md
id_to_name    ✗ banned
name_by_id    ✓ right
NAME-12

_indexed_by_ does not exist. Bare _by_ already names that shape.

naming_markers.md
users_indexed_by_id   ✗ does not exist
user_by_id            ✓ right
NAME-13

_grouped_by_ is retired from data names except for invariant plurals — fish, data, series — which cannot state cardinality by plurality. Prefer a countable noun when one exists.

var_names.md
fish_by_tank           // Record<tank, Fish>
fish_grouped_by_tank   // Record<tank, Fish[]>
rows_by_source         ✓ over data_by_source
NAME-14

_of_ is a possession query.

naming_markers.md
descendants_of(node)
NAME-15

is_ is a predicate and returns a boolean.

naming_markers.md
is_ancestor(a, b)
NAME-16

A standalone conversion and the variable it fills share their first word.

naming_markers.md
const json = json_from_tree(tree);
NAME-17

Naming is domain-first. Functions and files follow items_*, item_* or domain nouns; generic names are avoided.

FORMATTING.md
items_index_by_uid()   ✓ right
process() handle() util()   ✗ avoid
NAME-18

main is the single exception to domain-first naming — reserved for the entry function of an executable script.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
    report_print();
}

VARVariablesA name states the shape of its data.

VAR-01

A variable name states the shape of its data.

var_names.md
users                  // User[]
user_by_id             // Record<id, User>
users_by_role          // Record<role, User[]>
items_sorted_by_time   // Item[], reordered
VAR-02

If a variable is used in a return statement, it must be named out — return out;, exactly.

return_out.md
function emails_from_users(users)
{
    const out = [];
    for (const user of users) {
        if (user.email) {
            out.push(user.email);
        }
    }
    return out;
}
VAR-03

out never leaves the function. The caller names the result by what it means.

return_out.md
const emails = emails_from_users(users);
const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);
VAR-04

Returning a literal or an expression directly is allowed; a guard return may return null, false, [], {}. const out = {...}; return out; is rewritten as return {...};

FORMATTING.md
const out = {a, b};
return out;          ✗ rewrite this

return {a, b};       ✓ as this
VAR-05

The variable holding a caught error is always named error — in try/catch, in .catch(...), and in error event handlers alike.

var_names_error.md
catch (error) {
    console.log(error.message);
}

server.on('error', function (error) {
    throw error;
});
VAR-06

e, err and ex do not exist.

var_names_error.md
catch (e)     ✗ no
catch (err)   ✗ no
catch (error) ✓ yes
VAR-07

Accumulated stderr text is not an error variable. Name it by what it is.

var_names_error.md
stderr   ✓ right
err      ✗ wrong
VAR-08

Prefer explicit temporaries. Use intermediate variables instead of nested expressions; favor clarity over terseness.

FORMATTING.md
VAR-09

A lambda parameter is named v; a nested one is vv.

FORMATTING.md
items.map(v => v.uid)
items.some(v => v.sizes.some(vv => vv.width > 100))
VAR-10

The for...of loop variable is the singular of the collection.

for_of.md
for (const user of users) { }
for (const child of node.children) { }
VAR-11

A cached array length in a single loop is named end.

for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md
for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i < end; ++i) {
}
VAR-12

In nested loops the cached bound is the doubled index name: i → ii, j → jj, k → kk.

for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md
for (let i = 0, ii = foo.length; i < ii; ++i) {
    for (let j = 0, jj = bar.length; j < jj; ++j) {
        for (let k = 0, kk = baz.length; k < kk; ++k) {
        }
    }
}
VAR-13

Only that variable is out. A value that is joined, stringified or otherwise transformed on its way out is not out; it is named by what it is.

return_out.md
function csv_from_rows(rows)
{
    const lines = [];
    for (const row of rows) {
        lines.push(row.join(','));
    }
    return lines.join('\n');
}

FNFunction contractsWhat a prefix promises the caller.

FN-01

format_* returns a string intended for human display.

format_xxx.md
format_bytes(1457664)    // "1.4 MB"
format_duration(155000)  // "2m 35s"
format_usd(1299)         // "$12.99"
FN-02

A display conversion is never hand-rolled at a call site — an inline one is a missed format_*.

format_xxx.md
${Math.round(bytes / 1024)}kB   ✗ missed call
format_bytes(bytes)             ✓ right
FN-03

format_* returns — it never prints. Output is the caller’s job.

format_xxx.md
console.log(format_tree(tree));
FN-04

format_* is not for machine formats. Serialization is conversion, not display.

format_xxx.md
format_user(user)     // "Vladimir B. (admin)" — humans
json_from_user(user)  // machines
FN-05

render_* derives a small value — usually a string — from the object’s own state. The Vue analogy is a computed property, written as a method.

render_xxx.md
public function render_name_email()
{
    if ($this->name) {
        return sprintf('%s <%s>', $this->name, $this->email);
    }
    return $this->email;
}
FN-06

The prefix separates derived values from stored attributes. render_* is recomputed per call — never cached, never stored.

render_xxx.md
$this->email                  // a column
$this->render_dashboard_url() // computed every call
FN-07

render_* may return null when not applicable, and may throw when the state makes the value meaningless.

render_xxx.md
if (!$this->partner_email) {
    return null;
}
FN-08

render_* is never async and never side-effectful. A downloadable, substantial artifact — a zip, a csv, an xlsx — is export_*, which may be both.

render_xxx.md
$user->render_name_email()   // small, sync, pure
export_zip()                 // artifact, may be async
FN-09

format_* transforms an input it is given; render_* derives from self.

format_xxx.md
format_usd($cents)          // value in  → string out
$user->render_name_email()  // state in  → string out
FN-10

Anything that holds a local copy of remote data has refresh() — it pulls the data and brings the local vars up to date. Mental model: the browser refresh button.

refresh.md
refresh: async function () {
    await Promise.all([
        this.refresh_user(),
        this.refresh_banners(),
    ]);
},
FN-11

refresh() is idempotent — safe to call at any moment, any number of times.

refresh.md
FN-12

A fine-grained refresh_<part>() syncs one part of the state; refresh() composes them.

refresh.md
refresh_user: async function () {
    this.user = await fetch_user();
},
FN-13

Init is the first refresh.

refresh.md
mounted: async function () {
    await this.refresh();
    this.ready = true;
},
FN-14

An interaction — modal, popover — executes its own logic and returns a boolean commit flag. It expresses intent; it does not expose control flow.

interactions-should-return-only-boolean-flag.md
// true  → changes were committed
// false → no-op (cancel, or no changes)
if (await modal_upload().promise()) {
    await blocking(this.refresh());
}
FN-15

Guards return early. Validate inputs immediately and return null or empty values explicitly.

FORMATTING.md
FN-16

One public entry function per file.

FORMATTING.md

FMTFormattingBraces, breaks, blank lines, comments.

FMT-01

Indentation is exactly 4 spaces. No tabs.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-02

A top-level function declaration puts its opening brace on the next line.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
}
FMT-03

A function declared inside another function keeps its opening brace on the declaration line.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
    function limit_print(limit) {
    }
}
FMT-04

Function expressions, callbacks and Promise executors keep the opening brace on the declaration line.

formatting_blocks.md
server.on('error', function (error) {
});

return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
});
FMT-05

A class declaration puts its brace on the next line; its methods keep the brace on the declaration line.

formatting_blocks.md
class Logger
{
    constructor(parent_group_uid) {
    }

    write(format, ...values) {
    }
}
FMT-06

Module-level if, for and while keep the brace on the statement line.

formatting_blocks.md
if (process.env.DEBUG) {
}

for (const size of sizes) {
}
FMT-07

Always use braces for if, else, for, while. No single-line bodies.

FORMATTING.md
if (!user) return null;   ✗ no

if (!user) {              ✓ yes
    return null;
}
FMT-08

else starts on a new line.

FORMATTING.md
if (a) {
}
else if (b) {
}
else {
}
FMT-09

catch and finally start on a new line.

formatting_blocks.md
try {
}
catch (error) {
}
finally {
}
FMT-10

switch and case are aligned at the same indentation level.

FORMATTING.md
switch (type) {
case 'voice':
    break;
case 'text':
    break;
default:
}
FMT-11

A multi-line object literal holds one field per line, trailing comma included.

formatting_blocks.md
const next = {
    uid: item.uid,
    parent_uid: item.parent_uid,
    index,
};
FMT-12

An object of methods — Vue options style — spells each method as a function expression.

formatting_blocks.md
const options = {
    refresh: async function () {
    },
    render_name: function () {
    },
};
FMT-13

Keep an expression on one line when it fits on one line.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-14

Never split an assignment after = when its right-hand side is a single function call.

FORMATTING.md
const users_by_role =
    users_group_by_role(users);   ✗ no

const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);   ✓ yes
FMT-15

Break a statement only when its size or nested structure makes the break necessary. Line breaks must expose structure.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-16

A blank line marks a phase change — nothing else. Add one only when the following statement begins an independent conceptual step.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-17

Keep setup adjacent to the loop, condition or call that immediately uses it. Tightly coupled setup and use are not separated merely because the statement type changes.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-18

Construct an object from the required fields only. Do not spread a full object when a subset is needed.

FORMATTING.md
{...item, index}                              ✗ bad
{uid: item.uid, parent_uid: item.parent_uid, index}   ✓ good
FMT-19

Comments explain intent or policy only. No comments for obvious mechanics.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-20

A multi-line comment carries a rule, an invariant or a guarantee.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-21

Every route function carries a route comment directly above it: METHOD /path (params).

endpoint_comment.md
// GET /file/<name>
async function file_get(req, res)
{
}
FMT-22

Parentheses appear only when the endpoint takes input — body, headers, query, comma-separated, in that order.

endpoint_comment.md
// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)
function upload_post(req, res)
{
}
FMT-23

A header is prefixed with header:; a path parameter is spelled in the path itself.

endpoint_comment.md
header:x-filename
/file/<name>
FMT-24

An intent comment continues the same block on the next line.

endpoint_comment.md
// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)
// Streams to data/ before the body is fully read.
FMT-25

Every named function — top-level or nested — is a function name(...) declaration.

FORMATTING.md
function report_print()
{
}

FLOWControl flowImperative, explicit, no magic.

FLOW-01

Prefer imperative control flow.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-02

Prefer for...of when the index is not needed.

for_of.md
for (const item of items) {
}
FLOW-03

Use an indexed loop when the index is needed.

for_of.md
for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i < end; ++i) {
}
FLOW-04

do { ... } while (...) does not exist. Use while or for.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-05

reduce, deep chaining and functional pipelines are allowed only if the entire expression fits on a single line.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-06

Do not use arrow functions for non-trivial logic. Arrows are allowed only for tiny callbacks.

FORMATTING.md
const uids = items.map(v => v.uid);
fresh.catch(ignore);
FLOW-07

An arrow with a block body does not exist — it becomes function (...) {}, with an optional _this inside.

formatting_blocks.md
req.on('end', async () => {          ✗ does not exist
});

req.on('end', async function () {     ✓ this
});
FLOW-08

A catch that ignores the error binds nothing.

formatting_blocks.md
try {
}
catch {
}
FLOW-09

Use plain data structures — Set, Map or plain {} for lookups. No classes, no prototypes, no mutation via shared state.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-10

No implicit magic. No hidden side effects, no reliance on execution-order side effects.

FORMATTING.md

FILEFile and module structureOne entry function, one fixed order.

FILE-01

A library module exports one function, with module.exports at the end of the file.

FORMATTING.md
module.exports = items_index_by_uid;
FILE-02

An executable script uses main as its entry function and does not export.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-03

Do not combine a library export and an executable invocation in the same file.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-04

An executable hands its entry function to cli. cli owns the process contract: it keeps the event loop alive until main settles, reports a failure, and exits non-zero — ExitCodeError picks the code, any other error exits 1.

cli_main.md
const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');

cli(main);

async function main()
{
}
FILE-05

cli(main), never cli(main()). cli runs the function through Promise.try, so a synchronous throw is reported like a rejection; an already-invoked main() is a promise, and Promise.try rejects it with “expecting a function” — the app dies at startup.

cli_main.md
cli(main);     ✓ right
cli(main());   ✗ dies at startup
FILE-06

A hand-rolled main().catch(...) with process.exit(1) does not exist.

cli_main.md
main().catch(function (error) {
    console.error(error);
    process.exit(1);
});                              ✗ does not exist
FILE-07

An executable script may start with a shebang; nothing may precede it.

FORMATTING.md
#!/usr/bin/env node
FILE-08

The import block is sorted as plain text lines in byte order — what vim’s :sort over the block, or LC_ALL=C sort, produces. require and import alike.

FORMATTING.md
const $ = require('jquery');
const Vue = require('vue');
const axios = require('axios');
const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');
const fs = require('fs');
const {promisify} = require('util');
FILE-09

The whole line is the sort key — const or import included, not the module path and not the variable name.

imports_sorted.md
FILE-10

Byte order, not locale order: @ and $ come before letters, uppercase before lowercase, and { after z — destructured imports land last.

imports_sorted.md
const Vue = require('vue');       ← V before a
const axios = require('axios');
const {promisify} = require('util'); ← { after z
FILE-11

The import block is one contiguous list: no groups for builtins, packages and local files, and no blank lines or comments inside it — either one breaks the sort.

imports_sorted.md
FILE-12

File-level constants and variables follow the require statements.

FORMATTING.md
const report_limit = 31;
FILE-13

cli(main); comes immediately after all global initialization, and no executable code other than that call may appear before the public entry function.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-14

The public entry function is the first function in the file. In an executable, the first function declaration is function main().

FORMATTING.md
FILE-15

Helpers are defined after the public entry function, and before a library’s final export.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-16

Helpers must be named functions, not inline lambdas.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-17

CommonJS modules only. Use const <name> = require('<module>'); — never import or export.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-18

Library order is fixed.

FORMATTING.md
requires → constants → public entry → helpers → module.exports
FILE-19

Executable order is fixed.

FORMATTING.md
shebang → requires → globals → cli(main); → main() → helpers
FILE-20

A file exports exactly one thing, as its last statement, and is named after it. The rule is the same for both module systems: module.exports = name; or export default name;.

one_export_per_file.md
// items_index_by_uid.js
export default items_index_by_uid;
FILE-21

No named exports — and the consuming side is banned as well: several names are never taken from a local module. Several functions are several files, each named after its function.

one_export_per_file.md
export {engine_run, engine_transport};                   ✗ no
import {engine_run, engine_transport} from './engine';   ✗ no

import engine_run from './engine_run';                   ✓ yes
import engine_transport from './engine_transport';
FILE-22

A module which is a set of operations on shared state is one object with one default export. The callers reach the operations through the object — engine.run(prompt).

one_export_per_file.md
const engine = {
    transport: null,
    run: async function (prompt) {
    },
};

export default engine;
FILE-23

Research, scratch and test-support code inside a repository is not exempt from one export per file.

one_export_per_file.md
FILE-24

A named import from a library is the library’s shape, and a file whose shape is dictated by a tool follows the tool — module.exports.mochaHooks in a mocha hooks file.

one_export_per_file.md
import {mapState} from 'vuex';

PROJProject layoutA directory is a program; bin/ holds its verbs.

PROJ-01

Every project keeps one shape. A directory is a program, and bin/ holds its methods — one executable per verb, working the same in every language.

layout.md
bin/build      bb
bin/configure
bin/release
bin/run        rr
bin/test       tt
bin/watch      ww
PROJ-02

bin/configure is the only command to run after git pull to make a checkout ready for development.

layout.md
PROJ-03

In a node.js project run, test, build and watch are thin wrappers over npm. The wrappers still earn their keep: rr, tt, bb, ww are shorter than any npm form, and the names hold for projects that are not node.js.

layout.md
alias rr='bin/run'
alias tt='bin/test'
alias bb='bin/build'
alias ww='bin/watch'
PROJ-04

build/ holds what bin/build produced. Never committed, always reproducible.

layout.md
PROJ-05

data/ holds runtime state. Never committed.

layout.md
data/logs/2026-08-24.txt
PROJ-06

.env holds local values and is never committed. .env.example documents the expected keys and is.

layout.md
PROJ-07

Configuration lives in config/, is populated once when the project is set up, and code reads it through one path.

layout.md
const config = require('../config');
PROJ-08

src/ holds one subdirectory per part of the program.

layout.md
src/agent/    src/http/
src/android/  src/parser/
src/desktop-electron/
PROJ-09

Small shared functions go to src/helpers/, one function per file.

layout.md
src/helpers/array_group.js
PROJ-10

A unit test sits next to the file it tests.

layout.md
src/helpers/array_group.js
src/helpers/array_group.test.js
PROJ-11

tests/ holds suites that drive the whole program, such as playwright.

layout.md
PROJ-12

README.md stays short: what the project is and how to start it.

layout.md
PROJ-13

docs/ holds the official documentation, notes/ holds working notes — hints and findings made during development — and img/ holds static images, mostly for the README.

layout.md
PROJ-14

The project root carries the same standard files.

layout.md
.env  .env.example  .gitignore  Dockerfile
LICENSE  README.md  package.json
PROJ-15

Every bash script follows bin/templ: strict mode, the script / scriptdir / scriptname diagnostics, a temporary directory removed by an EXIT trap, and a colored exit message that starts as failed and is switched to succeeded on the last line.

templ
set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail

EXIT_MESSAGE="${RED}bin/templ failed${RESET}"

tempdir=`mktemp -d -t tmp.XXXXXXXXXX`
trap 'rm -rf $tempdir; echo -e "$EXIT_MESSAGE"' EXIT
cd $tempdir

EXIT_MESSAGE="${GREEN}bin/templ succeeded${RESET}"

LOGLogsOne line, one event, three fields.

LOG-01

A log is one infinite file. One physical line records one event, in three fields and nothing else.

logs.md
[time][group_uid][sender] details
LOG-02

Elapsed time, status and every other measurement belong in details, not in a fourth field.

logs.md
[cd8e5vqp][db_query_end_error] 30.001s ETIMEDOUT
LOG-03

time is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds.

logs.md
2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z
LOG-04

Include time when writing directly to a file; omit it when the runtime already timestamps the line, as docker does.

logs.md
[2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z][cd8e5vqp][db_query_begin] name=select_users
[cd8e5vqp][db_query_begin] name=select_users
LOG-05

A group is one unit of work — a request, a job, a cron run. Every event carries its group’s uid, an opaque string, usually a cuid.

logs.md
LOG-06

The first event of a group is group_spawn, emitted synchronously before the uid is passed to other work or another event is emitted for the group. A root group omits parent=.

logs.md
[new_group_uid][group_spawn] parent=old_group_uid
[c1a0root][group_spawn]
LOG-07

Messages and requests carry the caller’s uid; the receiver uses it as the parent of its new group.

logs.md
LOG-08

sender identifies one logging call site, and the name is unique in the whole codebase — a grep for it lands on one place. Think of it as a const in a single namespace.

logs.md
LOG-09

sender is snake_case.

logs.md
^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$
LOG-10

A _begin event is closed by the same stem with _end_ok or _end_error, in the same group. An end never appears without its begin in that group.

logs.md
[c9k2vf3p][mp4gif_worker_begin]
[c9k2vf3p][mp4gif_worker_end_ok] 4.512s

[c7t0xb1m][mp4gif_worker_begin]
[c7t0xb1m][mp4gif_worker_end_error] 0.884s ffmpeg exit=1
LOG-11

Use _end when the logged outcome — an HTTP status, say — already says what happened and classifying it as ok or error would mislead.

logs.md
LOG-12

A group costs at least three lines. Spawn one only when the work earns them: seconds of work, or many logging call sites. Do not spawn a group for one short call.

logs.md
[bbb][group_spawn] parent=aaa
[bbb][process_begin]
[bbb][process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise
LOG-13

Log short work on the caller’s group instead. When nothing is reported between the two ends, record one event.

logs.md
[aaa][process_begin]
[aaa][process_end_ok] 0.000s

[aaa][process_handled] 0.000s     ✓ even better
LOG-14

Two lines are the same noise when a new group holds a lone end. The matching begin was emitted on the parent — keep the pair there.

logs.md
[bbb][group_spawn] parent=aaa
[bbb][process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise
LOG-15

details are human-readable and terse, and never contain a physical newline.

logs.md
LOG-16

details never contain secrets, tokens, signed URLs, URL query values, bodies or headers. Prefer a reference to the payload over the payload.

logs.md
LOG-17

A printable ASCII word without spaces, double quotes, backslashes or square brackets is written bare — exactly the bytes that were sent, so it cannot span words, break the line, or mint a fake tag. Every other string is JSON-quoted.

logs.md
name=select_users
reason="db timeout"
value=""
LOG-18

Arrays, objects, booleans and null use compact JSON.

logs.md
retry=true limits={"soft":10,"hard":25}
LOG-19

An unordered list is sorted and prefixed with its count. Ordered values are not sorted.

logs.md
3:[180,783,846]
2:["bar","foo"]
0:[]
LOG-20

Truncation preserves valid UTF-8 and ends with the number of omitted bytes.

logs.md
...+4821
LOG-21

Keep one log line under 2k UTF-8 bytes. A log line describes an event; it is not payload storage.

logs.md
LOG-22

group_exit is optional and mainly serves to detect leaks. After it is emitted, no producer emits another event for that group; a parent may emit it for work it abandons. Consumers must accept groups without it — its absence makes no claim.

logs.md
[group_uid][group_exit]
LOG-23

“After” group_exit means producer emission order, not timestamp or collector ingestion order. Buffering may deliver an older event later; that alone is not an error. Without a causal-order signal — preserved per-group order, a shared sequence — cross-process detection is advisory.

logs.md

CSSClasses and stylesA fixed class order; every class has a rule.

CSS-01

Classes inside one class="…" attribute keep a fixed order. Plain utilities lead; an app-prefixed class (vb-*, np-* — one prefix per app, app-* in these examples) sorts after all of them, base class included; a file-local #-* class is always last.

css_classes.md
layout  spacing  sizing  decoration  typography  app-prefix  local

<div class="flex-row-c #-root" />
<div class="fluid p30 xpt app-scrollbars-light #-grid" />
<div class="db w80 h80 br4 fit-cover cur-pointer app-background #-preset-img" />
<div class="flex-row-cl gap10 app-font-b14 #-title-trigger" />
CSS-02

Within the utilities: a display or position utility (db, abs) leads where the element carries one, a gap* always comes directly after the layout class it belongs to, ph* precedes pv*, and spacing comes before typography.

css_classes.md
flex-row-c gap5
flex-col-c gap15
grid-foo gap5
CSS-03

Every class either has a rule in the file’s own style block or is an established project utility. An element that needs no styling stays classless — a label-only class rots and sends the next reader looking for a rule nobody wrote.

css_classes.md
<!-- the wrapper is not styled, so it carries no class -->
<div>
    <div class="#-funnel-bars">...</div>
</div>
CSS-04

gap* spaces the children of a grid or flex container; mg* and mi* are the block-container forms. The two do not mix.

css_classes.md
CSS-05

fluid marks the filling child of an hsplit/vsplit (whose children default to flex: none); flex-fluid marks the growing child of a plain flex-row/flex-col. Same CSS — the choice states which container the element sits in.

css_classes.md
CSS-06

An x* class usually comes before the setter it clears the way for — the broad class leads and the narrow one corrects it, whichever of the two is the reset.

css_classes.md
<div class="xm ml5" />   <!-- margin: 0; margin-left: 5px; -->
<div class="m5 xml" />   <!-- margin: 5px; margin-left: 0;  -->
CSS-07

Rows and columns are a <table>, not a stack of flex rows — the columns line up only until one cell is wider. Flex rows stay for content that is genuinely not tabular.

css_classes.md
CSS-08

@import comes first in a block; @include comes first in a rule, ahead of the property declarations — the mixin brings the base, the block overrides it.

css_classes.md
.#-card
    @include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)
    box-sizing: border-box
CSS-09

A transition: property is not written by hand — @include app-transition(props…) fills it, expanding each property into <prop> <speed> against the one shared speed. app-transition-fast and app-transition-debug are the same mixin at the fast and debug speeds. List the exact properties that change, never all, and put the include on the base rule rather than the state variant, so the animation covers both directions.

css_classes.md
@include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)
CSS-10

What each family holds: layout is the flex/grid/split class; spacing is p* / m*; sizing is w* / h* / max-w* / min-h*; decoration is br*, fit-cover, cur-pointer and the other shape and surface utilities; typography is fs* fw* lh*, then alignment and nowrap.

css_classes.md

VUEVue 2Components that behave like the platform.

VUE-01

Every component is provided with four global methods through a mixin.

vue-globals.md
px(value)        // format a pixel value
uid([name])      // ids unique across components
emit_end(retval) // return a value from a modal
emit_input(v)    // return a value from an input
VUE-02

Generated ids are bound to the current element and are what id and label[for] use. The name uid was chosen so it does not conflict with the id attribute every element may carry.

vue-globals.md
uid: function (name) {
    return name ? `c${this._uid}_${name}` : `c${this._uid}`;
},
VUE-03

Spell out v-on and v-bind. The shorthands @ and : are not used.

vue-formatting.md
<img v-bind:src="banner.thumbnail_url" v-bind:alt="banner.title" />
VUE-04

Attributes keep one order.

vue-formatting.md
ref v-if v-for v-on v-bind:ref v-bind [...] class type placeholder title
VUE-05

Avoid v-if and v-for on the same component — lift the condition to a <template>.

vue-formatting.md
<template v-if="items">
    <div v-for="item in items" v-bind:key="item.uid">
        {{ item.title }}
    </div>
</template>
VUE-06

A simple directive value stays bare; a compound one is wrapped in parentheses. Every directive — v-if, v-else-if, v-show, v-on, v-bind. Simple is a single identifier, member access, method call, template literal or unary negation; compound is anything carrying a binary operator or a ternary.

vue-formatting.md
<template v-if="is_ready">
<template v-if="(is_loading_fonts || is_loading_images)">
<div v-bind:class="(compact ? 'narrow' : 'wide')" />
VUE-07

Anything which takes data from a user is called an input and must work as a normal INPUT element.

vue-input.md
  1. takes data from the value property
  2. emits an input event
  3. respects the disabled state
  4. respects the readonly attribute
  5. reacts to clicks on the associated LABEL
  6. reacts to mouse hover from that LABEL
  7. injects and uses app_form_input_id
  8. takes focus with the TAB key
VUE-08

Avoid generic inputs — those with a lot of properties like min, max, step.

vue-input.md
VUE-09

Compose forms from app-form-div and app-form-label.

vue-form.md
<app-form-div class="flex-row mi10">
    <app-input-label>Email:</app-input-label>
    <app-input-email v-model="user.email" />
</app-form-div>
VUE-10

A form’s buttons close the form: cancel returns false through emit_end, submit is a type="submit" button.

vue-form.md
<app-button-orange v-on:click="emit_end(false)">
    Cancel
</app-button-orange>
<app-button-green type="submit">
    Submit
</app-button-green>
VUE-11

One button, one class.

vue-button.md
VUE-12

A slider is a container and a thumb. Position the thumb with top or left from 0 to 100% — 0 means empty, 100% means full.

vue-slider.md
left: 0      // empty
left: 100%   // full
VUE-13

Each SVG icon goes into its own svg-icon-*.vue file, containing only a TEMPLATE element with an SVG inside.

vue-svg-icon.md
<template>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
        <path fill="currentColor" d="..." />
    </svg>
</template>
VUE-14

SVG icons respect the currentColor CSS property.

vue-svg-icon.md
<path fill="currentColor" d="..." />
VUE-15

Component options keep one order.

vue-components.md
props inject provide mixins data computed watch methods mounted created beforeDestroy
VUE-16

An event handler is named after the UI part it is bound to — the event, then the button text.

vue-components.md
<button v-on:click="click_approve">
    Approve
</button>
VUE-17

A handler on an icon is named after the icon.

vue-components.md
<button v-on:click="click_icon_archive">
    <svg-icon-archive />
</button>
VUE-18

After the text or icon is changed, rename the corresponding event handler.

vue-components.md
Approve → Accept     // click_approve → click_accept

UIUser interfaceWhat every new screen carries.

UI-01

Every new UI — a SPA, an app screen, a report, a standalone HTML page — carries a visible light/dark switch. No exceptions: a page that only follows prefers-color-scheme has no switch, and does not count.

theme_switch.md
UI-02

The switch has exactly two states, Light and Dark. There is no System, Auto or follow-the-OS option, not even as the default.

theme_switch.md
UI-03

The light palette lives on bare :root; the dark one redefines the same tokens under :root[data-theme="dark"].

theme_switch.md
:root {
    --color-bg: #FFFFFF;
    --color-text: #1B1F23;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
    --color-bg: #15181C;
    --color-text: #E6E8EB;
}
UI-04

The root element is always stamped with data-theme="light" or data-theme="dark" — on load, before the first paint. The initial value comes from localStorage; with nothing stored, prefers-color-scheme is read once. The choice is saved back, and both the read and the write sit in try/catch.

theme_switch.md
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme;
UI-05

On a long page with a sticky bar, a second copy of the switch is docked at the far right of that bar — after any count label, not before it. It is shown only while the header one is off screen, and collapses to zero width otherwise.

theme_switch.md

RELPackaging and releaseShip a prebuilt dist/.

REL-01

Distribute a prebuilt dist/ from the repository, the way Vue, VueRouter, Vuex, jQuery, Bootstrap, Axios, Cuid and Jsondiffpatch do.

packaging.md
<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@2.6.11/dist/vue.js"></script>
REL-02

The release workflow is fixed: ensure there are no changes, increase the version, update dist/, commit, tag.

packaging.md
rm -rf dist
npm run build
git add package.json package-lock.json dist
git commit -m "release v$(...)"
git tag v$(...)
REL-03

Bump the version without committing or tagging, then own both steps in the script.

packaging.md
npm version $1 --git=/bin/true
REL-04

bin/release major|minor|patch performs the whole release.

packaging.md
bin/release patch
REL-05

A release script runs under bash strict mode.

packaging.md
set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail
REL-06

A bad argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1.

packaging.md
echo usage: release 'major|minor|patch' >&2
exit 1

DOCWriting the rulesHow a document in this repo is built.

DOC-01

A document has two halves. The author writes the top half, compressed around what he already knows; the AI writes the bottom half, restating it for a reader who lacks that context.

WRITING.md
DOC-02

The top half is the source of truth. When the halves disagree, the top half is right.

WRITING.md
DOC-03

No AI patches the top half. The one exception is an explicit request from the author.

WRITING.md
DOC-04

The bottom half is never edited in place. After the top half changes, it is regenerated from it.

WRITING.md
DOC-05

Most of the time the bottom half starts with a # heading, and that heading is the boundary. A --- line or a closing fence before it is decoration. There is no strict marker.

WRITING.md
--- ✨ AI-Generated Content Below ✨ ---
DOC-06

The report of a full audit is one file, notes/audit-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md. The projects have no issue tracker: the finding register of the newest audit note is the issue list, and later audits refer to findings by their ids.

audit_note.md
notes/audit-2026-09-02.md
DOC-07

An audit note keeps one order: title, repository line, scope, verdict with a health-at-a-glance table, finding register, findings, what is good, recommended order of work, status of prior findings, file inventory.

audit_note.md
DOC-08

The scope lists every check actually run, and what was not exercised. A check which was not run is said so; it is never implied.

audit_note.md
DOC-09

A finding id is <PROJECT>-NN, never reused and never renumbered. Each finding is one section citing file:line and the evidence — the quoted lines, the command which was run and what it printed.

audit_note.md
### RULES-01 Classes banned in one file, shown in another (high)
DOC-10

An audit note is written by the AI as a whole, so it has no top half and no separator. It is left untracked; it is committed only on request.

audit_note.md

LINTStated by the linterRules that only LINTING.md and the preset spell out.

LINT-01

Multiplicative operators are tight — *, /, **. Every other binary, logical and assignment operator has a space on each side.

LINTING.md
const x = a*b + c/d - e**2;
const x = a % 2;
LINT-02

An anonymous function has a space before its parenthesis; a named one has none.

LINTING.md
server.on('error', function (error) {
});

function main()
{
}
LINT-03

A tiny arrow is a single-line expression callback, passed as a call argument or as an object property value. It fits one line; the number of parameters does not matter. A lone parameter is v, nested vv; in a .catch it is error. It is taken whole — v => v.uid, not ({uid}) => uid. A named helper is a function declaration.

LINTING.md
LINT-04

forEach does not exist. Use for...of.

LINTING.md
items.forEach(function (item) {   ✗ no
});

for (const item of items) {       ✓ yes
}
LINT-05

The one class that may exist is a class that extends another.

LINTING.md
LINT-06

Imports are the first statements of a file, one statement per line. Side-effect imports — import './x', a bare require('x') — form their own block at the top, kept in the order they run; one blank line may separate it from the sorted named imports.

LINTING.md
LINT-07

Module format is the consuming project’s choice: JavaScript defaults to ES modules, .cjs is CommonJS, and the sorting rule supports both import forms. CommonJS-only is this repository’s own rule.

LINTING.md
LINT-08

gap* closes the layout group: the flex/grid/split container, then its flex-* modifiers, then the gap. Put a layout and its gap in the same class value.

LINTING.md
LINT-09

Within typography, fs* and fw* come before lh*. Several local #-* classes together form the final group.

LINTING.md
LINT-10

#- is written only in the forms the hashtag loader replaces: a double-quoted class, card_class or attribute ending in -class / :class; .#- in a style block; and the exact single-quoted '.#- form in JavaScript.

LINTING.md
LINT-11

Each statically known #-* class has a nonempty style selector in the same component. Declarations, includes and extends count as styles; an empty rule, a variable-only rule, or a mention inside :not(...) does not.

LINTING.md
LINT-12

A Vue <script> is indented four spaces with one base indent.

LINTING.md

No rule matches that.

In the canonical forms, ✓ and ✗ are verdicts, not code. The same index as a plain table: rules.md The words: The Glossaries github.com/vbarbarosh/rules
